© 2022 Rockwell Automation, Inc. All Rights Reserved / Author: Buol, Scott 
2 Project Overview 
Key Objectives and Benefits 
The Dallas, TX M3 Fill Finish Line owned by Mark Cuban Cost Plus Drug Company, PBC is a 
pharmaceutical production line adhering to FDA requirements.  
The new SCADA and PCS Misc. PLC system that will be installed in the M3 Fill Finish Line at Mark 
Cuban Cost Plus Drug Company, PBC, performs limited control, collects environmental data, and 
collects data from six production machines.  The SCADA and PCS Misc. PLC system will interface with 
the production machines and their various brands of PLCs.  
The SCADA system hardware consists of the following server and clients: 
 PCS Physical Servers: located in the Data Room (Room 056, Grid: C1-C2). 
 Client 1: Engineering Workstation PC located in Room 054 Grid: A4. 
 Client 2: Touchscreen PC used for operator interaction with associated PLC panel for 
control located in Utilities Room (Room 035 Grid: B2). 
 Client 3 (Group): Wireless Tablet PCs used for operator interaction with the process 
located within wireless coverage area on the site. 
The supervisory software will be deli vered and configured by  MAVERICK Technologies.   All servers and 
clients’ hardware will be installed and connected to the network by Mark Cuban Cost Plus Drug 
Company, PBC.  The communication between the server and the Ethernet distribution switch in the Data Room will be established through copper Ethernet cabling and from there, local Ethernet cabling will connect the different clients and PLC’s.  The wireless tablet PCs will connect to the servers in the Data Room via wireless access points throughout the facility.   
Project Assumptions, Conventions and Limitations 
This document assumes that the Customer has a basic understanding of, and familiarity with Rockwell 
Automation’s FactoryTalk View Site Edition (SE) functionality. 
The following limitations and assumptions are known: 
1. Per RFI-001, the recipe system requirements do not apply to the SCADA and PCS MISC. 
PLC System. 
2. In the September 14, 2021 meeting, MC CPDC approved a change from NEMA 4X to 
NEMA 12 since the panel is now located in a general use, non-washdown area.  UR4.5.2 
[URS-PCS-HR-014] Electrical enclosures shall be washdown duty, NEMA 4X rated no longer applies.  The chosen panel with rating of NEMA 4 exceeds the rating requirement of NEMA 12, thus satisfying the requirement.

2 Project Overview 
Key Objectives and Benefits 
The Dallas, TX M3 Fill Finish Line owned by Mark Cuban Cost Plus Drug Company, PBC is a 
pharmaceutical production line adhering to FDA requirements.  
The new SCADA and PCS Misc. PLC system that will be installed in the M3 Fill Finish Line at Mark 
Cuban Cost Plus Drug Company, PBC, performs limited control, collects environmental data, and 
collects data from six production machines.  The SCADA and PCS Misc. PLC system will interface with 
the production machines and their various brands of PLCs.  
The SCADA system hardware consists of the following server and clients: 
 PCS Physical Servers: located in the Data Room (Room 056, Grid: C1-C2). 
 Client 1: Engineering Workstation PC located in Room 054 Grid: A4. 
 Client 2: Touchscreen PC used for operator interaction with associated PLC panel for 
control located in Utilities Room (Room 035 Grid: B2). 
 Client 3 (Group): Wireless Tablet PCs used for operator interaction with the process 
located within wireless coverage area on the site. 
The supervisory software will be deli vered and configured by  MAVERICK Technologies.   All servers and 
clients’ hardware will be installed and connected to the network by Mark Cuban Cost Plus Drug 
Company, PBC.  The communication between the server and the Ethernet distribution switch in the Data Room will be established through copper Ethernet cabling and from there, local Ethernet cabling will connect the different clients and PLC’s.  The wireless tablet PCs will connect to the servers in the Data Room via wireless access points throughout the facility.   
Project Assumptions, Conventions and Limitations 
This document assumes that the Customer has a basic understanding of, and familiarity with Rockwell 
Automation’s FactoryTalk View Site Edition (SE) functionality. 
The following limitations and assumptions are known: 
1. Per RFI-001, the recipe system requirements do not apply to the SCADA and PCS MISC. 
PLC System. 
2. In the September 14, 2021 meeting, MC CPDC approved a change from NEMA 4X to 
NEMA 12 since the panel is now located in a general use, non-washdown area.  UR4.5.2 
[URS-PCS-HR-014] Electrical enclosures shall be washdown duty, NEMA 4X rated no longer applies.  The chosen panel with rating of NEMA 4 exceeds the rating requirement of NEMA 12, thus satisfying the requirement.

Automation’s FactoryTalk View Studio programming software to perform online and offline changes to the HMI screens and configuration files.  (Also discussed in Section 7.1.1.) 
The printer connected to the Engineering Workstation meets the requirement for printing.

12.3” screen, charger, IP65 stainless steel housing with carrying handle suitable for operation in GMP cleanrooms.

 F01.08: PCS Miscellaneous PLC Panel and Construction 
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR4.3.3 [URS-PCS-HR-003] The PCS Miscellaneous PLC Panel shall have no power source greater than 
50V except in the dedicated UPS compartment. The PLC panel shall not require Personal 
Protection Equipment (PPE) for arc flash dur ing maintenance and calibration. The panel 
shall be properly labeled to indicate this condition.  
UR4.5.2 [URS-PCS-HR-014] Electrical enclosur es shall be washdown duty, NEMA 4X rated.  
UR4.5.7 [MCCPDC 7.2.3] The SI shall provide PCS Miscellaneous PLC Panel Heat Load Calculation & 
Electrical Loading Calcs. These calculations  shall be maintained through to the final 
validated state As-Builts.  
 
A Hoffman panel with part number: A74H6018LP3PT des cribes a steel, NEMA 4, free-standing, two-
door enclosure.  This Hoffm an enclosure and the MAVERICK par tition design allows for the 
existence of a “lower voltage area” and a “higher voltage area”.  The high voltage area is a separate 
compartment that isolates the power source and components which have voltages higher than 50V.  In this way, a user can open the door for the lower voltage area to perform maintenance and calibration activities and will not be exposed to higher voltages which satisfies this requirement.  A sticker indicating the high voltage side will be affixed to the panel.  A sticker indicating the low voltage side will be affixed to the panel. 
In the September 14, 2021 meeting, MCCPDC approved a change from NEMA 4X to NEMA 12 
since the panel is now located in a general use, non-washdown area.  UR4.5.2 [URS-PCS-HR-014] Electrical enclosures shall be washdown duty, NEMA 4X rated no longer applies.  The chosen panel with rating of NEMA 4 exceeds the rating requirem ent of NEMA 12, thus satisfying the requirement. 
The heat load calculations were performed, and appropriate ventilation was specified to ensure no 
component exceeds its recommended operating window. 
 
 F01.09: Uninterruptible Power Supply System (UPS) 
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR4.3.4 [MCCPDC 3.2.2] The PCS Miscellaneous PL C panel shall have a UPS battery back-up system 
installed.     
UR4.3.5 [MCCPDC 3.2.2] The PCS Miscellaneous PL C panel UPS shall be capable of supplying the 
connected system power for at least fifteen (15)  minutes of operation after loss of facility 
electrical power.       
 
The selected Hoffman free standing two-door enclosure and the MAVER ICK partition design also 
allow for the placement of an Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) System on the high voltage side.  
The Tripp Lite UPS Model: SU2200XLA has been sized appropriately to power the connected system for the fifteen (15) minute duration as specified.

S-SR-037] All data comm unication shall be via Ethernet (protocol).  
 
In the PCS MISC. control panel, an access layer Stratix Ethernet switch provides connectivity for the 
PLC and the local HMI station.  The PLC and HMI communicate via the Ethernet/IP protocol over CAT6/CAT6A cabling. 
PCS MISC. access layer switch for the local PLC and local HMI provides 100Base-T 
communications (100 Megabit), not gigabit transfer rates.  Gigabit transfer rates are not applicable to 
this PLC and this HMI. Project: Mark Cuban Cost Plus Drug Company, PBC – 
 MCCPDC - SCADA and PCS MISC. PLC System

 F01.08: PCS Miscellaneous PLC Panel and Construction 
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR4.3.3 [URS-PCS-HR-003] The PCS Miscellaneous PLC Panel shall have no power source greater than 
50V except in the dedicated UPS compartment. The PLC panel shall not require Personal 
Protection Equipment (PPE) for arc flash dur ing maintenance and calibration. The panel 
shall be properly labeled to indicate this condition.  
UR4.5.2 [URS-PCS-HR-014] Electrical enclosur es shall be washdown duty, NEMA 4X rated.  
UR4.5.7 [MCCPDC 7.2.3] The SI shall provide PCS Miscellaneous PLC Panel Heat Load Calculation & 
Electrical Loading Calcs. These calculations  shall be maintained through to the final 
validated state As-Builts.  
 
A Hoffman panel with part number: A74H6018LP3PT des cribes a steel, NEMA 4, free-standing, two-
door enclosure.  This Hoffm an enclosure and the MAVERICK par tition design allows for the 
existence of a “lower voltage area” and a “higher voltage area”.  The high voltage area is a separate 
compartment that isolates the power source and components which have voltages higher than 50V.  In this way, a user can open the door for the lower voltage area to perform maintenance and calibration activities and will not be exposed to higher voltages which satisfies this requirement.  A sticker indicating the high voltage side will be affixed to the panel.  A sticker indicating the low voltage side will be affixed to the panel. 
In the September 14, 2021 meeting, MCCPDC approved a change from NEMA 4X to NEMA 12 
since the panel is now located in a general use, non-washdown area.  UR4.5.2 [URS-PCS-HR-014] Electrical enclosures shall be washdown duty, NEMA 4X rated no longer applies.  The chosen panel with rating of NEMA 4 exceeds the rating requirem ent of NEMA 12, thus satisfying the requirement. 
The heat load calculations were performed, and appropriate ventilation was specified to ensure no 
component exceeds its recommended operating window. 
 
 F01.09: Uninterruptible Power Supply System (UPS) 
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR4.3.4 [MCCPDC 3.2.2] The PCS Miscellaneous PL C panel shall have a UPS battery back-up system 
installed.     
UR4.3.5 [MCCPDC 3.2.2] The PCS Miscellaneous PL C panel UPS shall be capable of supplying the 
connected system power for at least fifteen (15)  minutes of operation after loss of facility 
electrical power.       
 
The selected Hoffman free standing two-door enclosure and the MAVER ICK partition design also 
allow for the placement of an Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) System on the high voltage side.  
The Tripp Lite UPS Model: SU2200XLA has been sized appropriately to power the connected system for the fifteen (15) minute duration as specified.

The Rockwell Software Factory Talk View SE platform shall be configured to make use of electronic 
signature features.  The delivered system has the Rockwell Software FactoryTalk View SE software loaded onto it, which hosts an operator interface application.  The delivered system has a custom operator interface application written for monitoring and, where appropriate, controlling the connected systems. 
 
The control system is programmed using control modules and follows the S88/S95 standards as 
applicable.  Process sequences have been programmed with steps and transitions as required, based on 
descriptions in the control logic narratives.   
 The Rockwell Software FactoryTalk View SE platform provides the ability to archive continuous process data, alarms, alarm acknowledgement, events, parameters, and ancillary data.  The alarm and events service saves all alarms and events in Universal Coordinated Time (UTC) 
without any time zone offsets or daylight savings adjustments added.  When the events are retrieved 
from the database for viewing, local time zone offsets or daylight savings adjustments can be applied.  In this way, the system does not lose any accuracy or data due to daylight savings or time zone offsets.    
The FactoryTalk Historian system reads data from the PCS-CP01 PLC and logs it appropriately. 
 The operator interface text will be displayed in English.

The Rockwell Software Factory Talk View SE platform shall be configured to make use of electronic 
signature features.  The delivered system has the Rockwell Software FactoryTalk View SE software loaded onto it, which hosts an operator interface application.  The delivered system has a custom operator interface application written for monitoring and, where appropriate, controlling the connected systems. 
 
The control system is programmed using control modules and follows the S88/S95 standards as 
applicable.  Process sequences have been programmed with steps and transitions as required, based on 
descriptions in the control logic narratives.   
 The Rockwell Software FactoryTalk View SE platform provides the ability to archive continuous process data, alarms, alarm acknowledgement, events, parameters, and ancillary data.  The alarm and events service saves all alarms and events in Universal Coordinated Time (UTC) 
without any time zone offsets or daylight savings adjustments added.  When the events are retrieved 
from the database for viewing, local time zone offsets or daylight savings adjustments can be applied.  In this way, the system does not lose any accuracy or data due to daylight savings or time zone offsets.    
The FactoryTalk Historian system reads data from the PCS-CP01 PLC and logs it appropriately.

 F05.01: Trending 
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR5.2.19 [URS-PCS-SR-025] Real-time multi-pen trends  for all analog and defined discrete signals.  Also, 
PID loop controller screens to include trending for PV, SP and CV as applicable.  
 
The system provides the ability to trend any of the tags in the PCS-CP01 PLC controller which 
includes both analog and discrete signals.  Tags can be added and removed at runtime.  The 
trending requirement for the PV, SP, and CV of the PID loops does not apply since there are no PID 
loops under the control of the PCS-CP01 system.   
 F05.02: Display colors of dynamic objects 
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR5.2.20 [URS-PCS-SR-026] The following colors shall be utilized when indicat ing states of dynamic 
objects…(see below)  
 
The following colors shall be utilized when indicating states of dynamic objects:  1. Gray – General meaning is “Not Operating” (e.g., motor not running, device is de-
energized, valve is closed).  
2. Green – General meaning is “Operating” (e.g., motor is running, device is energized, 
valve is open.). 
3. Yellow – General meaning is “Warning” or “Take Note” (e.g., device is in a mode 
other than normal such as manual mode, valve is in an intermediate state such as 
manual mode, valve is in an intermediate state such as traveling between closed and open).  
4. Red – General meaning is “Alarm” or “Lockout” (e.g., an alarm is active on a device or 
Operation, lockout is activated).  
The color palette is applied to dynamic objects to reflect the colors shown above.

valve is open.).

other than normal such as manual mode, valve is in an intermediate state such as 
manual mode, valve is in an intermediate state such as traveling between closed and open).

Operation, lockout is activated).

 F05.03: Print Screen Function 
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR5.2.21 [URS-PCS-SR-027] The capability to generate an electronic or hard copy of any active display 
must be available via the Print Screen function.  
 
A Print Screen button visible on each display allows for the capture of that display for later review. 
 F05.04: Overview Screen 
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR5.2.23 [URS-PCS-SR-029] The system shall provi de an “Overview” screen on all physical OITs. The 
overview screen will display “view-only” da ta for all critical parameters, values and 
information across the system. De tails of the required overview  information to be determined 
during detailed design.  
 
An Overview Screen (Main) is provided which displays the critical parameters, values, and 
information as described in Section 3.1.12 Overview Screen below.  
 
 F05.05: Input State and Simulation Review Screen 
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR5.3.3 [URS-PCS-SR-032] All inputs shall provide st ate and simulation features . This shall be captured 
on a separate maintenance screen, accessible by Admin and Maintenance personnel.  
 
An Input State and Simulation Review screens are present which are only accessible to the 
Administrator and Maintenance login security levels.  These screens displays the state of the wired input (actual input) and the state of the simulated input and if the simulation function is active for that particular input (simulated state is what controller sees).    
Since an Administrator or Maintenance person may put any input point in SIMULATE and change its 
value, it is the responsibility of this person to supervise and adjust the manually inserted value for any 
points placed in SIMULATE.  Failure to properly supervise and adjust manually inserted values may cause incorrect control functions and may lead to equipment damage. 
 F05.06: PLC firmware version and OIT version available via HMI 
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR5.2.17 [USR-PCS-SR-023] The PLC revision will be addressed to a PLC register, and hard coded OIT 
revision shall be accessible via a main menu  selection to users with Administrator or 
Engineer security level privileges.

Logging of Alarms, Warning Messages and Errors is done in a database table of the centralized 
database.  
Interlocks are conditions which, when active, will cause the effected device to go to its fail-safe state.  
The device will not be able to be activated until the interlock condition clears or the device is placed in Manual mode to override the interlocks.  All interlocks shall have associated alarms. 
Safety interlocks may not be overridden in any mode.  Process interlocks may be overridden with appropriate access level. Trip conditions shall be locked out for safety.   
A screen named Alarm Details is available to view past alarms.

UR5.2.14 [URS-PCS-SR-020] Alarms shall be in one of the following categories- Unacknowledged (active 
or inactive), Acknowledged (active), and Acknowledged (cleared).

Level 1  Level 1 alarms serve as warni ng alarms and will be annunciated on

level. 
Level 2  Level 2 alarms will serve as operator action alarms and will be 
annunciated on the OIT’s and external indicator.

level. 
Level 3  Level 3 alarms shall be reserved for interlock or lockout actions and 
conditions causing se quences to immediately be deactivated and will

 Alarm limit values cannot be changed by user input.

 F10.02: FactoryTalk View SE Security 
 Use a password-protected screen saver.  To ensure that only operators with the proper 
credentials are accessing workstations in a closed system, a password-protected screen 
saver can be used on the FactoryTalk View SE Client terminals.  This system will take the recommended exception to this rule when critical process data must be displayed at all times.  In this case, a ‘view only’ user account will be logged in to display the status of production and alarm information.  
 Use the included DeskLock software feature to restrict operators’ access to the client’s 
operating system.  
 Disable switch to other applications since this opens access to other programs.  
 Disable ‘Allow display code debugging’  since this allows launching of the VBA editor, 
which is not secure. 
 Change the window properties of the FactoryTalk View SE Client to disable the title 
bar, the system menu, the close button, and the show diagnostics list.  Set the window to be maximized. 
 F10.03: Configure FactoryTalk View SE clients automatically login as DEFAULT user 
after a period of inactivity 
Since the system requires that critical operations  information be displayed at all times, the DEFAULT 
User (a user with ‘view only’ access) shall be logged in when a period of inactivity occurs.  This allows the read-only display of production and alarm information.  
FactoryTalk View SE clients can be configured to automatically log out after a specified 
period of time, however this feature does not subsequently permit the immediate and automatic login of another user (DEFAULT) as required.  To achieve the required actions, idle conditions will be detected and then the DEFAULT user will be logged in effectively logging out the current user.

bar, the system menu, the close button, and the show diagnostics list.  Set the window to be maximized. 
 F10.03: Configure FactoryTalk View SE clients automatically login as DEFAULT user 
after a period of inactivity 
Since the system requires that critical operations  information be displayed at all times, the DEFAULT 
User (a user with ‘view only’ access) shall be logged in when a period of inactivity occurs.  This allows the read-only display of production and alarm information.

period of time, however this feature does not subsequently permit the immediate and automatic login of another user (DEFAULT) as required.  To achieve the required actions, idle conditions will be detected and then the DEFAULT user will be logged in effectively logging out the current user.

UR5.2.5 [URS-PCS-SR-011] System must be capable of utilizing active directory. It must be possible to

Both Microsoft Windows domain security and the FactoryTalk System Administration tool can enable the 
creation of a unique login and password for each user. 
FactoryTalk View SE can use Microsoft Windows security to manage user accounts. Password 
expiration, password aging, password complexity  requirements, account expiration, disabling of 
accounts, lockout aftern invalid login attempts, and forcing a change of password on first login are all security features provided by both Microso ft Windows security and FactoryTalk Security. 
Procedures should be implemented to ensure that user IDs do not get deleted or reassigned.  It is 
recommended to disable user IDs rather than deleting them as a best practice. 
The customer’s management procedure should include the verification of the identity of an individual 
before sanctioning an individual’s electronic signature. 
Once a user has been sanctioned and a unique account with password has been created in the 
FactoryTalk View SE system, the user is required to enter his/ her login and password to access FactoryTalk View SE. This process validates the identity of the user to FactoryTalk View SE. 
FactoryTalk View SE requires two components for us er identification: a unique login ID and password. 
When using the FactoryTalk View SE electronic signature feature, both the user login ID and password 
are required to perform an action.  The FactoryTalk View SE electronic signature feature can be configured to display and record the meaning of the signature. It also allows for separate performer and approval signatures, and for comments to be added regarding the meaning of the signature. 
If the user logs out of FactoryTalk View SE and again requires access, the user must reenter the login ID 
and password.

 F11.01: Process Historian 
This system contains the Rockwell FactoryTalk Historian SE software and server which 
satisfies the requirement to collect and transfer data. 
 F11.02: Critical Data Records 
This system maintains the following critical runtime data records: 
 FactoryTalk View SE alarm log and activity log data are stored in the corresponding 
databases as analog, digital and string values.     
 Analog, digital and string device tags that are transferred from the PLC to the 
FactoryTalk View SE system. 
F12.00: Audit Trail 
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR3.3.1 Every time a critical alarm threshold is modified and audit trail record shall be generated.  The 
record shall contain the following fields  
1. Date and time stamps of the change 
2. Original threshold value 
3. Threshold value after change 
4. User ID of the individual who has changed the threshold value (performer) 
5. Full name of the individual who has changed the threshold value (performer) 
6. Meaning of signature (performer) 
7. User ID of the individual who has approved the change (approver) 
8. Full name of the individual who has approved the change (approver) 
9. Meaning of signature (approver).  
UR3.3.2 Every time a critical alarm condition occurs an audit trail record shall be generated with the 
following fields  
1. Alarm date and time stamps  
2. Alarm tag 3. Alarm value 
4. Alarm description 
5. A similar record shall be generated whenever a critical alarm condition returns to normal 
condition.

FactoryTalk View SE provides an electronic signature feature for capturing operator actions 
performed in the production system.  This feature is  available in an E-Signature control, as well 
as the native button, numeric, and string input objects. 
With the FactoryTalk View SE electronic signature feature, each entry into the FactoryTalk View 
SE activity log is identified with: 
 time and date the action occurred, 
 name of the logged-in operator who performed the action, 
 terminal the action was performed from, 
 type of operation that was performed, and 
 value of the changed item before and after the change. 
When electronic signatures are used, the operator’s username and full name are also included. 
 The Critical Alarm Threshold Change Audit Trail entry will contain the following information: 
 Date and time stamps of the change 
 Original threshold value 
 Threshold value after change 
 User ID of the individual who has changed the threshold value (performer) 
 Full name of the individual who has changed the threshold value (performer) 
 Meaning of signature (performer) 
 User ID of the individual who has approved the change (approver) 
 Full name of the individual who has approved the change (approver) 
 Meaning of signature (approver). 
 
The Critical Alarm Audit Trail entry will contain the following information: 
 Alarm date and time stamps 
 Alarm tag 
 Alarm value 
 Alarm description 
 A similar record shall be generated whenever a critical alarm condition returns to 
normal condition.

F19.00: Availability 
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR3.2.2 Failur e/Recovery 
PLC/HMI 
The system shall have the means to reco ver from a hardware fault by means of 
reconfiguration and/or replacem ent and then reconfiguration. 
A list of hardware settings for each device shall be maintained as applicable. 
A list of software settings or suitable configurat ion file(s) for each device shall be maintained 
as applicable. 
Process Automation Control Server System 
The System shall have a means to recover from  software corruption or loss of configuration 
information by reprogramming or reloading of  the appropriate parameters. (Restore from 
backup)   
 
PLC/HMI 
 The PLC and HMI Systems store their programs onboard and, if configured to do so, recover 
from power failures and begin running again without the need for user intervention. 
 Recovery from software corruption is implemented via offline storage of the PLC and HMI 
software programs that is re-loaded to the devices should they become corrupted.  This is a restore from backup solution. 
 Process Automation Control Server System 
 The Process Automation Control Server System requires user action to start up the system 
after a shutdown.  Refer to the Rockwell Automation VersaVirtual™ Appliance User Manual (Publication GMSN-UM001_-EN-P) for instructions on the Start-Up procedure. 
F20.00: Redundancy 
The PLC logic program and the HMI program shall be stored in discrete memory devices which 
can be isolated (either physically or  electronically) from the rest of  the system to provide offline 
redundancy. 
 
Project: Mark Cuban Cost Plus Drug Company, PBC –

ID code: 215115305 -FS (V1.2) Page 52 of 58 
© 2022 Rockwell Automation, Inc. All Rights Reserved / Author: Buol, Scott 
Redundant PCS MISC PLC hardware is not present.  Should a significant enough failure occur to 
the PCS MISC PLC, the PLC will stop functioning and cease to control the process. 
For visualization, this system consists of one individual HMI terminal, three wireless tablets, and an 
HMI server hosting the display content.   
The individual HMI terminal mounted in the PCS CP01 cabinet does not have redundant 
hardware.  Should a significant enough failure occur to this HMI terminal, the HMI will stop 
functioning and not provide a working user interface.   
While there are three wireless tablets, which provides a means of redundancy due to multiple 
units, the individual tablets do not contain any redundant hardware.  Should one fail, the second or third unit would provide redundancy.   
The FactoryTalk View SE HMI server and other software is running on the VersaVirtual™ 
redundant hardware appliance and should one portion of the underlying hardware fail, the software 
will switch to the redundant hardware piece and continue providing service (screens and 
connectivity).   
As already mentioned, the VersaVirtual™ appliance has hardware redundancy built-in allowing a 
failure to occur and not interrupt the functions of the system (FactoryTalk View SE, Historian, FactoryTalk Security, etc.) 
F21.00: Maintainability 
 F21.01: Programming Software 
 
This function implements the following user requirement(s)  
UR5.1.1 [URS-PCS-SR-001] A SI provided Engineering Workstation perform online and offline changes to 
the PCS Miscellaneous PLC configuration and shall be capable of being connected to the 
OIT’s.     
 
Per Section 3.1.3 F01.03: Engineering Workstation, an Engineering Workstation is included which 
satisfies this requirement.   
Per 3.1.7 F01.07: Access Level Ethernet Switch the Ethernet switch is described which will allow 
connectivity from the Engineering workstation to the Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) satisfying 
the connectivity requirement. 
Per Section 2.1.1 Software, Rockwell Automation’s Studio 5000 Logix Designer software is available 
which is the Integrated Development Environment software permitting changes to all functions and 
features of the Programmable Logic Controller (PLC).  As noted in Section 3.1.3 this software is accessible to the Engineering Workstation via the ThinManager® technology. 
Per Section 2.1.1 Software, Rockwell Automation’s FactoryTalk View Studio programming software 
is available which is the Integrated Development Environment software permitting changes to all 
functions and features of the HMIs.  As noted in Section 3.1.3 this software is accessible to the Engineering Workstation via the ThinManager® technology.
